contest.text:
The contests take place near the Tree of Life, with care not to damage its roots, waterways, nearby wildlife or ritual grounds. A critic who demands that beauty justify itself is about to meet a village that disagrees.
Two cooks prepare meals from safely gathered foods. The feared judge announces, "If the Tree of Life could taste this, it would shed its leaves in protest." The crowd gasps; the judge insists (judge.he/she) meant the stew.
contest.name: The Roots and River Feast

a1.text: An ugly green dish proves magnificent.

a2.text: A catastrophically pungent pot drives everyone away from the feast; it is discarded and the cooks must start again.

b1.text: A modest cook beats the village favorite.

b2.text: The judge recognizes a childhood recipe and becomes emotional.

c1.text: The judges reward a cook who protected fragile plants.

c2.text: One ingredient is identified as unsafe and removed; no one eats it.
